## Task 1: Reflex Test {.unnumbered}

### What You Did

You caught a falling 30cm ruler five times. The distance you caught it at reflects your reaction time - shorter distance means faster reactions.

### Your Results


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![](activity_files/figure-html/reflex-plot-1.png){fig-align='center' width=672}
:::
:::


### Group Discussion Questions

**Q1.1** Look at the graph. What happens to performance from Trial 1 to Trial 5?

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Performance gets worse</option><option value='answer'>Performance improves</option><option value=''>Performance stays the same</option><option value=''>Performance is random</option></select>

**Q1.2** Were the **same people** tested in all 5 trials, or **different people** in each trial?

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Different people in each trial</option><option value='answer'>Same people in all trials</option></select>

**Q1.3** What design type is this? (See [within-subjects design](/glossary/design/within-groups-design.qmd))

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Between-subjects</option><option value='answer'>Within-subjects</option><option value=''>Correlational</option><option value=''>Matched pairs</option></select>

**Q1.4** What is the [**Independent Variable (IV)**](/glossary/design/independent-variable.qmd)?

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Trial number (1, 2, 3, 4, 5)</option><option value=''>Distance caught</option><option value=''>Reaction time</option><option value=''>Nothing - no IV</option></select>

**Q1.5** What is the [**Dependent Variable (DV)**](/glossary/design/dependent-variable.qmd)?

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Trial number</option><option value='answer'>Distance caught (or reaction time)</option><option value=''>The participant</option><option value=''>The ruler</option></select>

**Q1.6** Write a **one-tailed hypothesis** for this experiment:

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Example Answer
"Reaction time will decrease (improve) from Trial 1 to Trial 5" OR "Catch distance will decrease from Trial 1 to Trial 5"

This is a **practice effect** - performance improves with repetition.
:::

## Task 2: Time Warp {.unnumbered}

### What You Did

You estimated 60 seconds without counting. We wanted to see if people systematically over- or underestimate time.

### Your Results


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![](activity_files/figure-html/time-plot-1.png){fig-align='center' width=672}
:::
:::


### Group Discussion Questions

**Q2.1** On average, did people over- or underestimate 60 seconds?

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Overestimate (said 'stop' too late)</option><option value='answer'>Underestimate (said 'stop' too early)</option><option value=''>Perfectly accurate</option></select>

**Q2.2** What does it mean if someone underestimates 60 seconds?

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Time felt like it passed quickly (they thought 60s was up before it actually was)</option><option value=''>Time felt like it passed slowly</option><option value=''>They were counting accurately</option></select>

**Q2.3** This experiment compares people's estimates to a known target (60 seconds). The [**null hypothesis**](/glossary/statistics/) would be:

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Mean estimate will equal 60 seconds (no systematic bias)</option><option value=''>Mean estimate will be less than 60 seconds</option><option value=''>Mean estimate will be greater than 60 seconds</option><option value=''>There is no null hypothesis</option></select>

## Task 3: Memory {.unnumbered}

### The Secret Manipulation

Here's what you didn't know: **Lab A** and **Lab B** saw different words!

- **Lab A**: Abstract words (justice, freedom, wisdom...)
- **Lab B**: Concrete words (chair, river, mountain...)

### Your Results


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![](activity_files/figure-html/memory-plot-1.png){fig-align='center' width=672}
:::
:::


### Descriptive Statistics


::: {.cell}
::: {.cell-output-display}


Table: Memory scores by lab group

|Lab              |  n| Mean|   SD|
|:----------------|--:|----:|----:|
|Lab A (Abstract) | 13| 6.31| 1.89|
|Lab B (Concrete) | 15| 6.27| 1.98|


:::
:::


### Group Discussion Questions

**Q3.1** What is the [**Independent Variable (IV)**](/glossary/design/independent-variable.qmd)?

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Word type (abstract vs concrete)</option><option value=''>Number of words recalled</option><option value=''>The participant</option><option value=''>Memory ability</option></select>

**Q3.2** What is the [**Dependent Variable (DV)**](/glossary/design/dependent-variable.qmd)?

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Word type</option><option value='answer'>Number of words recalled</option><option value=''>Lab room</option><option value=''>Time to recall</option></select>

**Q3.3** Were the same people in both labs?

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Yes, same people saw both word types</option><option value='answer'>No, different people in each lab</option></select>

**Q3.4** What design type is this? (See [between-subjects design](/glossary/design/between-groups-design.qmd))

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Between-subjects</option><option value=''>Within-subjects</option><option value=''>Correlational</option><option value=''>Matched pairs</option></select>

**Q3.5** Write an **experimental hypothesis (H1)** - one-tailed:

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Concrete words will be recalled better than abstract words</option><option value=''>There will be no difference between word types</option><option value=''>Abstract words will be recalled better</option><option value=''>Word type will have some effect</option></select>

**Q3.6** Write a **null hypothesis (H0)**:

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Concrete words will be easier to remember</option><option value=''>Abstract words will be easier to remember</option><option value='answer'>There will be no difference in recall between word types</option><option value=''>Memory is always the same</option></select>

**Q3.7** Why might concrete words be easier to remember?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## The Answer: Dual Coding Theory
Concrete words can be stored in TWO ways: as a verbal code (the word) AND as a visual image (you can picture "chair"). Abstract words only have the verbal code. Two codes = better memory.
:::

## Task 4: Frontal Lob {.unnumbered}

### What You Did

You threw balls at a bucket:

- 10 throws with your **dominant hand**
- 5 throws with your **non-dominant hand**

### Your Results


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![](activity_files/figure-html/throwing-plot-1.png){fig-align='center' width=672}
:::
:::


### Group Discussion Questions

**Q4.1** Were the same people tested with both hands?

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>No, different people used different hands</option><option value='answer'>Yes, same people used both hands</option></select>

**Q4.2** What design type is this? (See [within-subjects design](/glossary/design/within-groups-design.qmd))

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Between-subjects</option><option value='answer'>Within-subjects</option><option value=''>Correlational</option><option value=''>Matched pairs</option></select>

**Q4.3** What is the [**IV**](/glossary/design/independent-variable.qmd)?

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Hand used (dominant vs non-dominant)</option><option value=''>Accuracy</option><option value=''>Number of throws</option><option value=''>The participant</option></select>

**Q4.4** What is the [**DV**](/glossary/design/dependent-variable.qmd)?

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Hand used</option><option value='answer'>Throwing accuracy (%)</option><option value=''>Number of attempts</option><option value=''>The bucket</option></select>

**Q4.5** Why is within-subjects design considered "more powerful"?

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>You need fewer participants</option><option value=''>The statistics are simpler</option><option value='answer'>Each person is their own control - individual differences are eliminated</option><option value=''>The results are always significant</option></select>

**Q4.6** Which statistical test would you use to compare dominant vs non-dominant hand?

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Independent t-test</option><option value='answer'>Paired t-test</option><option value=''>Correlation</option><option value=''>Chi-square</option></select>

## Task 5: Sleep & Memory {.unnumbered}

### The Question

Before the session, you told us how many hours you slept last night. We also measured how many words you recalled.

**Is there a relationship between sleep and memory?**

### Your Results


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![](activity_files/figure-html/sleep-memory-plot-1.png){fig-align='center' width=672}
:::
:::


### Group Discussion Questions

**Q5.1** Is there an IV in this study?

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Yes - sleep hours</option><option value=''>Yes - memory score</option><option value='answer'>No - we measured both variables, we didn't manipulate either</option><option value=''>Yes - the participant</option></select>

**Q5.2** What design type is this? (See [correlational design](/glossary/design/correlational-design.qmd))

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Between-subjects</option><option value=''>Within-subjects</option><option value='answer'>Correlational</option><option value=''>Experimental</option></select>

**Q5.3** What does a positive correlation mean here?

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Sleep causes better memory</option><option value='answer'>People who slept more tended to recall more words</option><option value=''>People who slept less recalled more words</option><option value=''>There is no relationship</option></select>

**Q5.4** Can we say that sleep **causes** better memory based on this data?

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>TRUE</option><option value='answer'>FALSE</option></select>

**Q5.5** Why can't we make causal claims from correlational data?

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>The sample was too small</option><option value=''>The correlation wasn't strong enough</option><option value='answer'>Third variables might explain the relationship (e.g., health, motivation)</option><option value=''>Correlations are always meaningless</option></select>

::: {.callout-warning}
## The Critical Point: Correlation ≠ Causation

Even if we find a relationship between sleep and memory, we **cannot** say sleep *causes* better memory. Why?

- Maybe healthier people sleep more AND have better memory
- Maybe motivated students prepare better (sleep AND study)
- Maybe stress reduces both sleep AND memory

This is why **experiments** (with manipulation) are needed to establish causation.
:::

## Task 6: Sixth Sense {.unnumbered}

### What You Did

6 trials: Someone either stared at you or didn't. You guessed which.

**If just guessing randomly**: You'd expect to get 3 out of 6 correct (50%).

### Your Results


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![](activity_files/figure-html/sixth-sense-plot-1.png){fig-align='center' width=672}
:::
:::


### Group Discussion Questions

**Q6.1** If someone got 5 out of 6 correct, does that **prove** they have a sixth sense?

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>TRUE</option><option value='answer'>FALSE</option></select>

**Q6.2** Why not?

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>5/6 is impossible</option><option value='answer'>Some people will get 5/6 just by luck, even without any real ability</option><option value=''>The experiment was designed wrong</option><option value=''>Sixth sense definitely doesn't exist</option></select>

**Q6.3** What does 50% accuracy suggest?

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>They definitely have a sixth sense</option><option value=''>They definitely don't have a sixth sense</option><option value='answer'>Performance is at chance level - consistent with random guessing</option><option value=''>The task was too hard</option></select>

**Q6.4** What is the **null hypothesis** for this study?

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>People can detect staring</option><option value=''>People cannot detect staring</option><option value='answer'>Detection accuracy equals 50% (chance level)</option><option value=''>There is no null hypothesis</option></select>

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Why Statistics Matter

With 28 people, **some will get lucky** just by chance. If everyone flipped a coin 6 times, someone would get 5 or 6 heads - but that doesn't mean their coin is biased!

**Statistics help us ask**: Is this result more extreme than we'd expect from chance alone?
:::

## Summary {.unnumbered}

::: {.callout-important}
## Key Concepts from Today

**Design Types** (See [glossary](/glossary/design/))

| Type | Same people? | IV? | Test to use | Example |
|------|-------------|-----|-------------|---------|
| [Between-subjects](/glossary/design/between-groups-design.qmd) | No | Yes | Independent t-test | Memory (Lab A vs B) |
| [Within-subjects](/glossary/design/within-groups-design.qmd) | Yes | Yes | Paired t-test | Throwing (Dom vs Non-dom) |
| [Correlational](/glossary/design/correlational-design.qmd) | N/A | No | Correlation | Sleep & Memory |

**Variables**

- [**IV (Independent Variable)**](/glossary/design/independent-variable.qmd): What the researcher manipulates or controls
- [**DV (Dependent Variable)**](/glossary/design/dependent-variable.qmd): What the researcher measures

**Hypotheses**

- **Experimental (H1)**: Predicts an effect or difference
- **Null (H0)**: Predicts no effect (any difference is due to chance)
- **One-tailed**: Specifies the direction ("A will be greater than B")
- **Two-tailed**: Just predicts a difference ("A and B will differ")
:::
